title: Multi-day long-duration energy storage
bottleneck: Wind and solar droughts can last days to weeks, but today's grid storage, overwhelmingly lithium-ion, is economic only up to about 4 hours. Multi-day storage technologies such as iron-air, hydrogen, and compressed air exist as pilots but have not demonstrated the combination of low capital cost, acceptable efficiency, and durability at grid scale. Without multi-day storage, deep decarbonization requires massive renewable overbuild or firm generation.
why_it_blocks: This is the central storage gap for a renewables-dominated grid. Short-duration batteries handle daily cycles, but weather-scale variability has no economic solution yet.
current_state: Iron-air and other long-duration pilots are under construction with DOE support. Costs and performance at scale remain unproven. DOE's long-duration storage programs are funding first commercial projects, but none have operated long enough to prove bankability.
